## c86f5a19e34d

**Reproduced teaching ambiguity; audit target left unchanged.** Current generator SHA-256 is `8478db35626694bd09fffdef3c6deede66ff41770998a651feaea0196446ba38`; executed rule hash is `f5d00e3992ee`.

The rival program is: transpose only when occupied nonzero cells occur on both sides of the main diagonal; otherwise return the input unchanged. It fits all 3 canonical pairs because each canonical input has occupied cells on both sides. For generated seed `100`, sample indices `0`, `1`, and `2` are also mixed-side, so the rival fits all three demonstrations. Sample index `3` is upper-side only: the authority transposes it, while the rival returns identity, producing 10 differing cells.

All seven inputs used in this evidence (three canonical plus four generated lesson pairs) pass the target’s `self_check`. The query is generated by the documented default domain with difficulty `None`; no private answer was guessed. Exact input, Racket output, rival output, per-cell differences, source identity, and lesson provenance are retained in `checks/audit/c86f5a19e34d/`.

The target battery completed with 10 green and 2 advisory stages. Semantic gate reported no executable contract, and override emitted a nonblocking legacy grid-validity warning. Evidence: `checks/audit/c86f5a19e34d-battery/checks/c86f5a19e34d_before_battery_summary.json`. The finding is semantic even though the structural battery has no failed stage: a legitimate three-demo lesson does not distinguish the authority from the rival.

Supported authority replay command: `python3 run_with_racket.py python3 -m arcpuzzles apply c86f5a19e34d --input ../checks/audit/c86f5a19e34d/input.json --out ../checks/audit/c86f5a19e34d/racket.json` from `packet_root/repo`.
